native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (Copper&Gold + Amber + Monument Count, Z-scores) peaked in the 14th-13th century BCE (1400-1300 BCE), where the two adjacent 100-year bins tie at a summed Z of 4.238, above the next-highest bins (1200/1100 BCE: 3.62; 2700 BCE: 2.96). The increase into the peak was driven by Copper&Gold (ZCU_AU, i.e., gold/copper), which jumped from -0.36 to +2.54 (delta +2.90) between the 1500 and 1400 BCE bins after a flat near-baseline (-0.6 to -0.36) for 4300-1500 BCE, approaching its all-time maximum (2.85 in 1200/1100 BCE), and by Monument Count (ZMonument), which rose from +0.17 to +1.71 (delta +1.54) in the same transition (its all-time maximum of 3.95 occurred earlier, at 2700 BCE). Amber (Zamber) was roughly flat (-0.15 to -0.01, delta +0.14) and contributed little. Thus the late 2nd-millennium BCE social-capital peak was driven primarily by copper&gold and by monument count, with amber essentially unchanged.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parsed capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300-500, pre-binned at exactly 100-year steps; comma-decimal values) with spot verification of parsed values against raw CSV strings; confirmed zero NaN in ZCU_AU, Zamber, ZMonument. 2) Summed the three social-capital Z-values per 100-year bin; located the maximum: 4.2381, a 2-bin tie at 1400 and 1300 BCE. 3) Computed per-component deltas from the 1500 to the 1400 BCE bin (CopperGold +2.90, MonumentCount +1.54, Amber +0.14) and full-range trend directions (CopperGold step-up from flat baseline, max 2.85 at 1200/1100 BCE; MonumentCount max 3.949 at 2700 BCE; Amber max 1.54 at 3300-3000 BCE). 4) Cross-checked against time_series_data.csv raw rows (CE=-X corresponds to BCE=X): 37 overlapping bins with 0 value mismatches, and its summed series peaks at the identical 4.2381 in the same two bins. 5) Robustness: including MonumentSize (ZMW) still yields the peak at 1400 BCE (4.904); the pollen/openness dataset contains no social-capital columns and plays no role. Executed script: analysis.py.
